question: What is the meaning of diameter in relation to general information?
description: The term "diameter" in the context of general information, particularly in relation to digitalization for circularity in construction, likely refers to the measurement of the width across a circular object or feature. In the context of materials passports (MPs) and digital twin technologies (DTs), diameter could be used to describe the size of components or materials, which is essential information for managing and tracking materials throughout their lifecycle. This data is crucial for achieving circularity in construction, as it allows for the efficient use, recycling, or disposal of materials.

3. Research methods 
This section outlines the methodologies used to conduct the study, 
each selected for its ability to meet the research objectives. The primary 
goal of the research is to identify the information requirements that 
constitute DPPs. To this end, a literature review was undertaken and 
presented in Section 3.1. Additionally, to understand the information 
requirements from industry perspectives, interviews were conducted 
and detailed in Section 3.2. The research further aims to develop 
ontology-based DPPs based on these identified information re­
quirements following the Modular Ontology Modeling (MOMo) meth­
odology, with the development process outlined in Section 3.3. 
3.1. Literature review 
A literature review was conducted to identify the IRs that constitute 
DPPs. This approach made it possible to reveal existing knowledge and 
findings related to what DPPs are and what information they should 
contain. A systematic search process outline by Booth et al. (2016) was 
followed to gather relevant papers. The databases Scopus and Web of 
Science, which are known for their extensive collections of peer- 
reviewed scientific papers (Leslie, 2013; Mongeon and Paul-Hus, 
2015), were employed to retrieve papers that are pertinent to the 
study of IRs for DPPs in the construction industry. Table 1 presents the 
search results including search strategy, databases, field and date. The 
search was conducted with no restrictions on the publication date 
considering the topic under study represents a recent development in 
research. The papers retrieved span from the years 2019 to 2023.
